payload.claim: Across 86 North American simulation studies, landscape fuel treatments consistently reduce wildfire extent and severity compared to untreated scenarios, but the degree of benefit is highly sensitive to treatment spatial arrangement, not just total treated area.
payload.title: Fuel treatment effectiveness at the landscape scale: a systematic review of simulation studies comparing treatment scenarios in North America
payload.summary: Systematic review of 86 simulation studies (200-3,400,000 ha) comparing fuel-treated vs untreated landscape scenarios. Most studies found reduced damaging fire with treatment, but effectiveness depended strongly on treatment design/configuration rather than area treated alone.

payload.claim: A 26-study empirical review found total treated area within a wildfire perimeter is highly correlated with wildfire area (r=0.89), but only 12 of 26 studies showed treatments affect fire behavior outside treatment boundaries, i.e. landscape-level spillover effects are far less established than site-level effects.
payload.title: A systematic review of empirical evidence for landscape-level fuel treatment effectiveness
payload.summary: Reviewed 26 empirical (not simulated) North American studies of wildfire-meets-treatment events over 30 years. Site-level effectiveness is robust; landscape-level (beyond-boundary) effectiveness evidence is thin and treatment-configuration dependent.

payload.claim: Optimal fuel treatment layouts that minimize total landscape fire loss form contiguous, regular spatial patterns whose shape shifts with the ignition-probability distribution and the spatial distribution of assets to protect, implying no single placement pattern (e.g. highest-load) is universally optimal across differing risk/asset layouts.
payload.title: Optimize landscape fuel treatment locations to create control opportunities for future fires
payload.summary: Mixed-integer-programming model igniting fire from every grid cell to find treatment placements minimizing total future fire loss. Found trade-offs between protecting different landscape areas are the dominant driver of optimal spatial layout, more so than any single fuel/asset metric.

payload.claim: A mixed-integer-programming optimizer for fuel-break placement within a landscape network, driven by large sets of simulated wildfires, produces significantly better reductions in fire size and WUI area burned than a rule-based (e.g. simple priority-ranking) placement heuristic in Southern California test cases.
payload.title: An optimization model to prioritize fuel treatments within a landscape fuel break network
payload.summary: MIP model prioritizes fuel breaks in an existing network using simulated-fire data, benchmarked against rule-based placement. Optimization-based placement beat heuristic/rule-based placement on both total fire size reduction and WUI area protected.

payload.claim: A fuel-break optimization framework combining burn-probability simulation, structural-loss modeling and network optimization found that even modest fuel-treatment budgets yield significant structure-loss risk reduction, and that placing breaks both inside and outside a single jurisdiction boundary outperforms single-jurisdiction placement.
payload.title: Optimizing fuel break placement to mitigate wildland fire risk to communities
payload.summary: Evaluated 198 scenarios varying budget and jurisdictional constraints around a military training base and surrounding communities. Cross-jurisdictional, network-optimized placement reduced structure-loss risk most, even at modest treatment budgets analogous to a fixed 5% budget regime.

payload.claim: Intensifying prescribed burning within the WUI reduces house-loss damages more than applying the same effort as landscape-wide (dispersed) treatment, but WUI-focused treatment is substantially more costly per unit area, creating a direct cost-effectiveness trade-off between asset-buffer and landscape-pattern strategies.
payload.title: Where to prescribe burn: the costs and benefits of prescribed burning close to houses
payload.summary: Compared landscape-wide vs WUI-concentrated prescribed-burn scenarios in southwest Western Australia using three independent models. WUI treatment gave greater damage reduction per area but at much higher cost, a pattern directly relevant to asset-buffer vs other placement strategies.

payload.claim: Across 1,617 wildfire-exposed houses in southern Australia, house destruction rates were significantly lower only where prior burning occurred within 5 years and less than 3 km upwind of the house, i.e. upwind-of-asset placement relative to the dominant wind at the time of the fire is a necessary condition for prescribed-burn effectiveness at protecting structures.
payload.title: The effectiveness of prescribed burning for protecting houses during wildfires in Australia
payload.summary: Empirical analysis of house-loss outcomes controlling for weather, terrain and near-house vegetation. Upwind-within-5-years-and-3km burning reduced house loss; most houses studied lacked such upwind treatment, and defensible space (vegetation within 40 m) was an even stronger predictor than upwind burning.

payload.claim: Cost-effective prescribed-burning strategies (edge-of-asset vs dispersed landscape burning) differ by landscape and by which asset class is being protected (houses, lives, transmission lines, carbon, ecology), so a placement pattern ranked best for one landscape/asset combination need not transfer to another landscape or wind regime.
payload.title: Cost-Effective Prescribed Burning Solutions Vary Between Landscapes in Eastern Australia

Best strategy varied by city/landscape, supporting the research question's concern about transferability across wind regimes.

payload.claim: A complex-network / centrality-based method for siting fuel breaks (targeting network nodes that most favor fire propagation) outperformed the conventional density/flammability-based placement benchmark in both an artificial forest landscape and a real Rhodes, Greece case study.
payload.title: A Complex Network Theory Approach for the Spatial Distribution of Fire Breaks in Heterogeneous Forest Landscapes for the Control of Wildland Fires
payload.summary: Models fire spread as a Markov field on a weighted directed network (weights from a cellular-automata fire model using GIS/meteorological data) and places fuel breaks at high-centrality nodes. This centrality approach beat a fuel-load/flammability-based placement rule in both simulated and real landscapes.

payload.claim: Fuel-treatment placement relative to forest cover type materially changes rate of spread, fire size and fire-type prevalence for decades after treatment, showing that *where* (not just how much) treatment is placed interacts with underlying landscape heterogeneity to determine long-term effectiveness.
payload.title: Long-Term Impacts of Fuel Treatment Placement with Respect to Forest Cover Type on Potential Fire Behavior across a Mountainous Landscape
payload.summary: Simulated 20%-of-landscape thinning placed exclusively on southerly vs northerly aspects in a 48 km2 Colorado landscape, tracking fire behavior for 50 years post-treatment. Placement relative to cover type/aspect produced persistently different spread, size and severity outcomes.

payload.summary:
Screen X2 (60 train scenarios: 20 ignitions x 3 weather, 720 sims) compared 6 strategies against a pooled 5-seed random-control baseline (burned_ha mean=779.6 ha, asset_cells mean=20.7) and a no-treatment control S0-5cada3. Pre-registered criterion: win = reduction >=10%, 95% CI of rel_change excludes 0 on the correct side, Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon p<0.05.

H1 path_centrality (S5-2af155), burned_ha, predicted -18%: OBSERVED +15.96% [CI -0.22, +31.03], p_holm=0.249 — burned_ha went UP, opposite of the predicted direction, and is not significant. On asset_cells, path_centrality was +65.27% [40.4, 93.7], p_holm=0.00097 ('worse') — statistically indistinguishable from the no-treatment control (none: +65.59%) and from burn_prob (+65.59%). Path-centrality placement did not transfer at all in this screen: it neither reduced burned area nor protected assets. REJECTED. High confidence, large surprise.

H2 hybrid (S6-54bc0a), burned_ha, predicted -20% AND must beat best single-criterion strategy: OBSERVED +13.57% [-3.06, +29.96], p_holm=0.475 — burned_ha increased, CI straddles zero, not significant, and opposite of predicted direction. It also fails the 'beats best single-criterion strategy' clause: fuel_load alone (S1-cddd29) was directionally better at -5.64% [-30.90, +19.11] (ns) than hybrid's +13.57%, even though hybrid beat burn_prob (+27.48%) and path_centrality (+15.96%). On asset_cells, hybrid delivered a real, significant win: -62.68% [-77.35, -46.61], p_holm=0.00097 — close to asset_buffer's result. So the hypothesis's secondary qualitative claim ('also cuts asset_cells substantially') is supported even though its primary quantitative burned_ha claim and the 'beats single-criterion' clause are not. REJECTED on primary metric/criterion (burned_ha); note partial support on asset_cells as a secondary, non-predicted finding. Medium confidence, surprising split result.

H3 asset_buffer (S3-1f12db), asset_cells, predicted -35%: OBSERVED -100.00% [-100.00, -99.9999996], p_holm=0.000086, verdict 'wins'. Effect size vastly exceeds the prediction (every asset cell protected across all 60 train scenarios, vs 20.7 baseline mean) — far stronger than hypothesized, itself a notable surprise (ceiling effect). On burned_ha, no improvement: +14.97% [-2.45, +32.53], ns — consistent with the hypothesis's own caveat that landscape-wide burned area would improve 'only modestly' (here, not at all, though not significantly worse either). One falsification sub-clause — 'upwind_weight=0.6 must beat an upwind_weight=0 asset_buffer run' — was NOT tested in this screen (no such arm exists among the 12 plans), so that part of the pre-registration is untested, not merely unmet. SUPPORTED on the stated primary criterion; the upwind-weight ablation remains open. High confidence on the tested claim, but reopen the ablation.

H4 wind_strips (S4-8ab95d), burned_ha, predicted -15%: OBSERVED -26.06% [-42.43, -11.60], p_wilcoxon=0.0085, p_holm=0.05095. Effect size and CI both clearly support the hypothesis (exceeds predicted magnitude, CI entirely below zero) -- but the Holm-adjusted p is 0.0509, just barely at/above the pre-registered 0.05 bar (falsified_if explicitly triggers at p_holm>=0.05). This is a hair's-breadth miss driven by multiple-comparison correction across the 6 simultaneous strategy tests, not by a weak or ambiguous effect. On asset_cells, wind_strips also won clearly: -61.07% [-76.50, -43.96], p_holm=0.00097. Calling this INCONCLUSIVE rather than a clean reject or accept: the point estimate and CI are compelling but the pre-registered significance bar is formally not cleared. Recommend a confirmatory replicate (more seeds/scenarios) before promoting or discarding. Low-to-medium confidence as stated; the underlying effect looks real.

Ranking across both metrics (screen-level, not final): wind_strips (best combined: large, if borderline-significant, burned_ha cut + strong asset protection) > asset_buffer (best asset protection, no burned_ha cost) > hybrid (strong asset protection, burned_ha cost) > fuel_load (small ns improvements both metrics) > path_centrality ~= burn_prob (no benefit or harmful, matching no-treatment) > none (worst, confirmed significantly worse than the random-control baseline on burned_ha: +62.95% [45.1,82.1], p_holm=1.1e-7 -- a useful sanity check that random cell placement already beats doing nothing).

RANDOM-CONTROL SEED SPREAD -- explicit assessment: the 5 random-control replicates (SR-3d4159, SR-decc78, SR-a679f6, SR-bbd12f, SR-44bf1e), run under IDENTICAL scenario sets (same 20 ignitions x 3 weather), show efficiency-vs-no-treatment ratios of 0.62, 0.65, 0.51, 0.72, and 0.99 -- i.e. one random seed (SR-44bf1e) barely beat doing nothing at all (1% effective reduction) while another (SR-a679f6) cut burned area to half of no-treatment (49% reduction). That is a ~2x spread in apparent 'random strategy' effectiveness driven purely by seed, which is as large as or larger than most of the hypothesized treatment effects (10-20%) this screen was built to detect. This is BOTH a surprise and a power problem for a 60-scenario screen: (a) surprise, because random placement was assumed to be a low-variance, interchangeable baseline, and it is not -- the pooled baseline_mean is sensitive to exactly which 5 seeds were drawn; (b) power problem, because this baseline noise plausibly explains why wind_strips' genuinely large, correctly-signed effect (-26%) landed at p_holm=0.051 instead of clearing 0.05 -- the correction is being paid for simultaneously testing 6 strategies against a baseline whose own seed-to-seed variance is substantial relative to n=60 scenarios. Recommend: widen the random-control seed pool (>5) and/or increase n_ignitions/n_weather before round 2's refine/deep test, and do not treat the current baseline_mean as a low-noise reference when deciding promotion thresholds.
reopen: H1: path_centrality strategy did not transfer -- increased burned_ha and matched no-treatment on asset_cells; revisit the centrality-targets-bottlenecks assumption (evidence E9/E11/E4) before further investment.

H2: hybrid did not beat the single-criterion fuel_load baseline on burned_ha and increased burned_ha outright; revisit hybrid weighting (less burn_prob/centrality weight?) or split H2 into separate burned_ha and asset_cells predictions since the two metrics diverged sharply.
H3: upwind_weight=0.6 vs upwind_weight=0 ablation was never run in this screen -- add it before fully crediting the upwind-weighting mechanism specifically (vs. asset_buffer placement generically).
H4: borderline p_holm=0.0509 on an otherwise compelling CI -- schedule a confirmatory replicate with more scenarios/seeds before promoting or dropping wind_strips.

Assumption that 5 random-control seeds under identical scenario sets form a stable, low-variance baseline is not supported (efficiency spread 0.51-0.99); revisit random-control sizing and baseline-variance reporting for all rounds, not just this one.

== CORRECTION TO F1 PER D1 ==
efficiency_vs_no_treatment is HIGHER-IS-BETTER (ratio reflecting lower burned area relative to no-treatment), not lower-is-better as F1 read it. Re-reading ST3's values with the correct direction: wind_strips spacing12 (1.307) > wind_strips spacing8 (1.040) > the 10 random-control seeds (0.737-1.073) > hybrid (0.717) > asset_buffer upwind0 (0.699) > asset_buffer upwind0.6 (0.672). This correctly tracks the burned_ha results below (wind_strips reduces burned area -> high efficiency; hybrid/asset_buffer increase it slightly -> low efficiency). F1's claim that SR-44bf1e 'barely beat doing nothing' was backwards: high efficiency = good performance, so that seed was actually the BEST-performing random draw in ST2, not the worst. Noted for the record so future findings don't repeat the inversion.

Control-seed spread with the larger pool: this round's 10 random seeds span efficiency 0.737-1.073 (ratio 1.46x) vs round 1's 5 seeds spanning 0.51-0.99 (ratio 1.94x, under the corrected direction). The spread shrank materially going from 5->10 seeds and 60->150 scenarios, which is exactly what D1's remedy predicted and is itself a (mild, expected) non-surprise confirming the round-1 power concern was real and partially fixed.

== H8 (primary): confirmatory wind_strips spacing=12, plus spacing=8 'denser is better' lever claim ==
Clause (i) confirm spacing=12: OBSERVED -29.60% [-37.27, -22.13], p_wilcoxon=2.26e-6, p_holm=1.13e-5, verdict 'wins'. This clears every bar (>=10% reduction, CI<0, Holm p<0.05) with a much tighter CI and far stronger significance than ST2's borderline p_holm=0.0509. CONFIRMED.
Clause (ii) spacing=8 must outperform spacing=12 on burned_ha: OBSERVED spacing=8 (S4-e85bdd) = -12.10% [-20.65, -3.38], p_wilcoxon=0.0337, p_holm=0.0423, verdict 'wins' in isolation (clears the bar against random control) but is far WEAKER than spacing=12's -29.60%, the opposite of the predicted ordering. The predicted -30% for the spacing=8 arm overshot the observed -12.10% by more than 2x, and the comparative claim ('denser is the key lever') is reversed, not just missed. Per H8's own OR-type falsified_if, this failure of clause (ii) falsifies the hypothesis as stated, despite clause (i) succeeding. REJECTED overall (observed_change_pct reported against the spacing=8 prediction it was built around), but note the valuable positive result: wind_strips spacing=12 is now a CONFIRMED LEADER under the pre-registered criterion on burned_ha, and also wins asset_cells (-59.16% [-67.53,-49.86], p_holm=1.29e-9) -- the best combined performer across both metrics and both rounds. High confidence on both the confirmation and the rejection of the spacing-lever claim.

== H6: hybrid asset_cells confirmatory, predicted -60% ==
OBSERVED -75.69% [-81.75, -68.76], p_wilcoxon=2.31e-12, p_holm=9.22e-12, verdict 'wins'. Exceeds the prediction and strongly reconfirms ST2's -62.68% with far tighter CI and power. SUPPORTED, high confidence. Side note: hybrid's burned_ha cost, which was a non-significant trend in ST2 (+13.57%, ns), is now statistically confirmed with more power: +9.02% [0.29, 18.91], p_holm=0.0423, verdict 'worse' -- a small but real, reliable burned-area penalty from the hybrid weighting, not noise.

== H7: asset_buffer upwind-weight ablation (upwind=0.6 vs upwind=0), predicted -95% for the upwind=0.6 arm ==
OBSERVED: both arms hit the exact same ceiling -- upwind=0.6 (S3-1f12db): -100.00% [-100.00,-100.00], p_holm=9.95e-13; upwind=0 (S3-b6e1e1): -100.00% [-100.00,-100.00], p_holm=9.95e-13. The two arms are tied to numerical precision (0 percentage-point gap), which is squarely inside H7's own falsification trigger ('upwind=0 arm within 5pp of upwind=0.6 arm'). REJECTED as a test of the upwind-weighting mechanism: asset_buffer's near-total asset protection at this landscape/budget comes from simple proximity to the small asset footprint, not from wind-aware orientation -- the E7-based directional mechanism adds no detectable marginal benefit here. This also looks like a ceiling/floor artifact: both arms hit -100% exactly, so the test had no room to show a difference even if one existed; it is uninformative about the mechanism beyond 'both suffice,' not strong evidence the mechanism is literally worthless in general. Observed magnitude (-100%) exceeds the -95% point prediction, so the quantitative prediction for the upwind=0.6 arm alone is technically met, but the comparative/mechanistic claim the hypothesis was actually designed to test is rejected.

== Is wind_strips spacing=12 now a confirmed leader? YES. == Clears all three pre-registered bars on burned_ha (-29.60%, CI entirely below zero, p_holm=1.13e-5 << 0.05) and independently wins asset_cells (-59.16%, p_holm=1.29e-9). It is the only strategy tested across both rounds that wins on both metrics without a documented side cost, and the round-1 borderline result is now decisively resolved in its favor.

H7: both upwind_weight arms hit an exact -100% ceiling, so the test could not discriminate the upwind mechanism from plain proximity -- rerun the ablation under a harder condition (lower budget_pct, larger/more dispersed asset footprint, or a heldout landscape) where asset_buffer does not trivially saturate, before concluding the E7 upwind mechanism is unnecessary in general.

== DOES S4-8ab95d STILL WIN? ==

payload.summary:
[Covers both round-4 blocks: EXP-R4-A / stats_id ST6 (train ignitions x train/SW(225) weather, seed 0, 300 scenarios) and EXP-R4-B / stats_id ST7 (heldout ignitions x heldout_nw(315) weather, FRESH seed 1, 50 ignitions x 6 weather = 300 scenarios, materially larger than round 3's 150).] Round 4 (V2, tests H9 primary/H10/H11) looks for a single fixed placement that wins on burned_ha under BOTH wind regimes. Integrity note per D3/V2: the SW/train block reuses the standard train generator -- a designated reusable refinement resource, not a held-out-integrity concern. The NW/heldout_nw block uses a fresh seed (1) and a larger draw (300 vs 150 scenarios) than EXP-R3-A/ST4's model-selection draw; V2 itself flags this is not guaranteed fully independent if the heldout generator is deterministic/nested, so treat it as a fresh-but-not-certified-independent replicate, not a from-scratch holdout.

== Per-arm, per-regime verdicts (criterion unchanged: >=10% reduction, CI excludes 0, Holm p<0.05) ==

S4-8ab95d (225, reference): Train/SW -- burned_ha -30.48% [-35.88,-25.03] p_holm=1.15e-9 WINS; asset_cells -55.73% [-62.33,-48.85] p_holm=2.03e-14 WINS. Heldout_nw/fresh-seed -- burned_ha -12.53% [-19.86,-5.30] p_holm=0.1000 NO_CLEAR_DIFFERENCE (fails); asset_cells -23.57% [-32.81,-14.20] p_holm=0.00021 WINS. Does NOT win both regimes (fails NW on its primary metric, burned_ha).

S4-f4f566 (270 strip, H9 primary): Train/SW -- burned_ha -15.32% [-21.10,-9.82] p_holm=4.05e-5 WINS; asset_cells +16.21% [5.62,27.08] p_holm=0.00135 WORSE (significantly harms asset protection under SW). Heldout_nw -- burned_ha -30.99% [-37.79,-24.38] p_holm=1.52e-11 WINS; asset_cells -45.50% [-56.43,-33.91] p_holm=3.17e-9 WINS. WINS BURNED_HA IN BOTH REGIMES -- the only arm to do so -- but at the cost of a significant asset_cells loss under train/SW.

S4-6c51bd (315 strip, H10): Train/SW -- burned_ha +1.44% [-5.40,8.16] p_holm=0.283 NO_CLEAR_DIFFERENCE; asset_cells +2.00% [-7.66,12.03] p_holm=0.242 NO_CLEAR_DIFFERENCE. Heldout_nw -- burned_ha -24.86% [-33.07,-16.67] p_holm=0.00137 WINS; asset_cells -43.19% [-54.68,-31.31] p_holm=2.53e-5 WINS. Does NOT win both regimes (fails train/SW on both metrics).

S6-eefd58 (hybrid 270, H11): Train/SW -- burned_ha +9.11% [3.00,15.69] p_holm=0.00072 WORSE (significantly harmful); asset_cells -62.09% [-67.96,-55.90] p_holm=1.11e-14 WINS. Heldout_nw -- burned_ha +4.59% [-3.45,12.13] p_holm=0.00033 but CI straddles zero -> NO_CLEAR_DIFFERENCE (see anomaly note below); asset_cells -60.56% [-67.04,-53.55] p_holm=3.39e-13 WINS. Does NOT win burned_ha in either regime (actively harmful in train/SW); asset protection remains robust in both.

== Best single fixed plan winning under BOTH wind directions? == On the primary objective (burned_ha): YES, S4-f4f566 (wind_strips, wind_from_deg=270) wins in both the train/SW and heldout_nw regimes, and is the ONLY arm that does so. However, no arm wins on BOTH metrics in BOTH regimes: S4-f4f566 trades away asset_cells performance under train/SW (+16.21%, significantly worse than random), while S4-8ab95d retains asset protection in both regimes but fails burned_ha under NW. Any recommendation of S4-f4f566 as 'the' direction-robust fixed plan must carry this asset-protection caveat for the SW regime explicitly.

== Does S4-8ab95d's fresh-seed heldout_nw result agree with EXP-R3-A/ST4? == YES, qualitatively and quantitatively consistent. ST4 (150 scenarios, seed 0): burned_ha -14.50% [-26.29,-2.97], p_holm=0.489, no_clear_difference; asset_cells -26.97% [-42.29,-10.15], p_holm=0.067, no_clear_difference (narrow miss). ST7 (300 scenarios, fresh seed 1): burned_ha -12.53% [-19.86,-5.30], p_holm=0.100, no_clear_difference (same verdict, similar point estimate, CI tightened, p_holm fell but still above 0.05); asset_cells -23.57% [-32.81,-14.20], p_holm=0.00021, now WINS (crossed into significance with the larger/fresh sample). The core finding -- S4-8ab95d fails to win burned_ha under NW wind -- replicates on an independent-ish, larger draw, reinforcing that round 3's result was a real regime effect, not a one-off artifact of the smaller sample; the asset_cells flip (ns -> significant win) shows that metric genuinely was underpowered at n=150, exactly as F3 flagged.

== H9/H10/H11: prediction vs observed ==
H9 (270 strip wins burned_ha in BOTH regimes, ~-20% each): OBSERVED train -15.32% (weaker than predicted, and only 0.32 percentage points past the hypothesis's own -15% stability floor -- a knife-edge pass) and heldout_nw -30.99% (much stronger than predicted, near the original 225-strip's peak train performance). SUPPORTED on the binary double-regime burned_ha win, but the symmetric ~-20%/-20% magnitude prediction was wrong in both directions (weaker at train, stronger at NW) and the train-block pass margin is thin. Flagging the asset_cells cost at train as an un-predicted side effect.
H10 (315 strip fails under train/SW, ~-14% ns, within 10pp of S4-8ab95d's -14.50% NW-mismatch number): OBSERVED +1.44% [-5.40,8.16], p_holm=0.283 -- correctly non-significant (qualitative prediction holds) but the point estimate (+1.44%) differs from -14.50% by about 16 percentage points, exceeding H10's own 10-point symmetry tolerance. REJECTED: the orientation-mismatch penalty is NOT symmetric between the two strip orientations -- 315-under-SW loses essentially its entire effect (near 0%), while 225-under-NW retains roughly half its peak effect (-12.5% to -14.5% of a ~-30% peak). This points to a landscape/asset-geometry anisotropy rather than a simple angular-mismatch model.
H11 (270 hybrid wins burned_ha in both regimes, ~-12% each, asset_cells >=50% both): OBSERVED train +9.11% [3.00,15.69], p_holm=0.00072, verdict 'worse' (significantly harmful, not just a missed win); heldout_nw +4.59% [-3.45,12.13], p_holm=0.00033, CI straddles zero -> no_clear_difference. REJECTED decisively on burned_ha in both regimes. Asset_cells side-claim supported in both (-62.09%, -60.56%, both >=50%).

== Statistical anomaly recurrence == S6-eefd58's heldout_nw burned_ha result reproduces the CI-vs-Holm-p disagreement F3 first flagged for S4-8ab95d: p_holm=0.00033 (highly significant by the rank test) while the bootstrap CI [-3.45,12.13] straddles zero. The lab's compute_stats tool resolves this conservatively (verdict follows CI-includes-zero -> no_clear_difference), which seems the right conservative default, but the recurrence across two different arms/rounds suggests this is a structural feature of the scenario-level difference distributions (likely heavy-tailed/skewed), not a one-off; it should be documented as a known criterion caveat rather than re-discovered each round.
reopen: The orientation-mismatch penalty is asymmetric between 225-under-NW (retains ~-12 to -14.5%) and 315-under-SW (collapses to ~0%) -- investigate what landscape/asset-geometry feature breaks the assumed angular symmetry before generalizing the 'bisector compromise' logic (H9) to other wind-regime pairs.

S4-f4f566 (the only double-regime burned_ha winner) significantly worsens asset_cells under train/SW (+16.21%, p_holm=0.00135) -- safety/director must decide whether a burned-area-robust-but-asset-costly plan is an acceptable recommendation, or whether a combined wind_strips+asset_buffer/hybrid deployment is needed to cover both objectives.

Document the recurring CI-vs-Holm-p disagreement (seen now for S4-8ab95d/ST4 and S6-eefd58/ST7) as a standing methodological caveat of the pre-registered criterion rather than treating each occurrence as a fresh surprise.

H11's hybrid-270 variant made burned_ha performance worse (not just unstable) relative to hybrid-225's prior null/mixed results -- re-centering the wind parameter did not stabilize it as hoped; reopen whether hybrid should be recommended for burned_ha at all (vs. being restricted to its asset_cells role).

No single plan wins on BOTH metrics in BOTH regimes -- before safety review, the director should decide whether the recommendation target is burned_ha-robustness (favoring S4-f4f566) or a dual-objective compromise (e.g. pairing S4-f4f566 or S4-8ab95d with an asset_buffer/hybrid overlay).

The earlier framing ('S4-f4f566 trades away asset protection under SW winds') should be narrowed to 'under the train ignition set at train-weather severity' pending further investigation, since the same wind direction under heldout ignitions + extreme severity does not reproduce the cost.

H9 (cumulative): originally predicted and tested for winning burned_ha under train and heldout_nw only; this block extends the same claim to heldout_extreme and it holds (-26.42%, clearing all three criterion bars). Cumulative verdict across the full test matrix: SUPPORTED, high confidence -- S4-f4f566 is confirmed as the only plan in the program that wins burned_ha under every regime tested.

S4-f4f566's asset_cells win under heldout_extreme is comparatively weak (-18.70%, p_holm=0.0175, barely past the 10%/0.05 bars) versus the reference's -38.04% in the same block -- if asset protection is a hard requirement (not just nice-to-have), the margin here is thinner than headline 'wins' framing suggests and should be flagged to safety_agent as a lower-confidence win relative to the reference.

Final recommendation choice (S4-f4f566 as the robust generalist vs. S4-8ab95d as the stronger specialist with one known NW failure mode) is a policy/risk-tolerance decision for the director and human, not a statistical one -- this finding supplies the effect sizes and CIs for that call but does not resolve it.

payload.description: Wind_strips treatments are oriented fuel breaks whose protective value in the simulator depends on fire spread arriving from close to the assumed wind_from_deg=270 direction. All burned_ha 'wins' (ST6/ST7/ST8) were produced by a fire-spread simulator under simulated weather draws, not by physical fire behavior; if real prescribed-burn operations or wildfire events encounter winds/conditions outside the narrow prescription envelope (rh 20-50%, wind 5-25 km/h, temp 5-30C) used to define feasible burn days, strip performance and crew control of the burn itself are unvalidated. No escape-probability or containment-failure modeling exists in this pipeline.
payload.mitigation: Require a conventional prescribed-burn burn plan with on-the-ground control lines, trigger points, and abort criteria before any implementation; treat the simulator's burned_ha reduction as a planning signal for strip placement only, not as a guarantee of control during ignition operations.

payload.description: Implementing wind_strips over 702 treated cells (5.0% of burnable area, 702 ha) implies prescribed-fire or mechanical treatment operations at scale; the lab has no smoke-dispersion, air-quality, or downwind-population model. Burn-window feasibility here is defined purely by fire-weather prescription (RH/wind/temp), not by air-quality permitting windows, which are frequently the binding constraint on prescribed burn days in practice.
payload.mitigation: Route implementation through standard air-quality/smoke-permit review (e.g. regional air district burn authorization) before scheduling; do not treat the burn_window_days count below as a permitted-burn-day count.

payload.description: The strip pattern (spacing 12, width 2, 5% of burnable area) and its ecological effects (habitat fragmentation, repeated-entry soil/vegetation impacts, effect on fire-dependent vs fire-sensitive species) are not represented in the simulator, which only scores burned_ha and asset_cells. payload.description: All evidence for S4-f4f566 comes from a synthetic landscape (synthetic_v1, a modeled Sierra-foothills-weather analogue, not a validated real site), from a simulator that treats treated cells as effectively non-burnable (a simplification of real fuel-break performance, which reduces but does not eliminate fire spread), and from simulated/resampled weather draws rather than observed fire events. Per F4, the heldout_nw scenario set uses a fresh seed but is 'not guaranteed fully independent' of the model-selection draw if the generator is deterministic/nested — so even the 'heldout' wins are not certified out-of-sample in the strictest sense.
payload.mitigation: Caveat every effect size in the recommendation as simulator-derived under a synthetic landscape; require field pilot validation (small-scale real treatment + monitoring) before scaling the 5% budget plan to an actual landscape.

payload.description: burn_window_days(region_id=synthetic_v1, default prescription RH 20-50%, wind 5-25 km/h, temp 5-30C, 10:00-17:00, >=4 consecutive qualifying hours) returns a mean of 145.0 feasible burn-weather days/year (sd 22.5; range 121-176 across 2021-2025), i.e. roughly 40% of the year meets the weather prescription, so weather is not a binding constraint in principle. However, feasible days cluster heavily in spring (Apr 19.6, May 21.4 days/month) and secondarily Sep-Oct (15.4, 16.4), with very few in peak/late summer (Jul 7.0, Aug 8.4) and almost none in Dec (0.8) or Jan (7.8) — so the practical implementation window for 702 ha of strip treatment is a few concentrated months per year, not a year-round option, and multi-year sequencing/crew capacity will determine how many seasons are needed to complete and maintain the strips.
payload.mitigation: Plan implementation across the Apr-May / Sep-Oct windows specifically rather than assuming 145 days are freely schedulable; budget multiple burn seasons for full build-out and for strip maintenance/re-entry, and re-run burn_window_days against the actual deployment site (not synthetic_v1) before scheduling.

payload.description: The 270-deg orientation tested in S4-f4f566 was conceived (H9) after seeing the round-3 NW/315-ish transfer failure of the 225-deg reference plan S4-8ab95d — i.e. it is a post-hoc hypothesis tuned to the observed failure mode, raising a mild HARKing/overfitting-to-known-regimes concern even though it was subsequently tested on fresh seeds across three regimes (ST6/ST7/ST8) and won burned_ha in all three. Additionally, the full train-ignitions x train/SW(moderate) x heldout-ignitions combination has never been run — only train-ignitions x train/SW (ST6) and heldout-ignitions x heldout_nw/heldout_extreme (ST7/ST8) have been tested, so the asset_cells cost and the burned_ha margin under moderate SW weather specifically on unseen ignition locations remain unverified.
payload.mitigation: Disclose the post-hoc derivation of the 270 orientation in the recommendation; run the named follow-up (heldout ignitions x train/moderate-SW weather, fresh seed, for S4-f4f566 vs S4-8ab95d) before treating the asset_cells trade-off as resolved, as D5 itself proposes as next-but-unaffordable work.

payload.caveats:
Scope: results come from a simplified simulator (firelab-ca-0.1) on the synthetic landscape synthetic_v1. They rank candidate placement rules for expert review; they are not burn prescriptions.

Recommendation: S4-f4f566 (wind_strips, spacing 12, width 2, priority burn_prob, oriented for wind_from_deg 270, 5% budget) is forwarded as the wind-direction-robust placement. It is the only plan in the program to win the pre-registered burned_ha criterion in all three regimes tested: train/SW -15.32% [-21.10, -9.82] (ST6), heldout_nw fresh seed -30.99% [-37.79, -24.38] (ST7), heldout_extreme fresh seed -26.42% [-34.40, -19.45] (ST8). The SW-specialist alternative S4-8ab95d (225 strips) has larger SW margins (ST6 -30.48%, ST8 -38.12%) but failed the NW transfer test twice (ST4 p_holm 0.489; ST7 p_holm 0.100).

1. Asset protection (R1, high): in train ignitions x train/SW weather, S4-f4f566 is significantly worse than random on asset_cells (+16.21%, 95% CI [5.62, 27.08], p_holm 0.0014, ST6). This did not reproduce under heldout_extreme (asset_cells -18.70%, narrow win, p_holm 0.0175, ST8) and it wins under heldout_nw (-45.50%, ST7). The cause is unconfirmed, and the plan was never tested on heldout ignitions under moderate SW weather, the scenario that would settle it.
2. Post-hoc design (R7, medium): the 270 orientation (hypothesis H9, agent-generated) was proposed after the 225 plan's NW failure, then evaluated only on fresh-seed scenarios. That is supportive, but some risk of overfitting to known regimes remains.
3. Model limits (R5, medium): synthetic landscape, treated cells modelled as effectively non-burnable, simulated weather; heldout draws are fresh-seeded but not certified fully independent of the selection draws.
4. Escape/control (R2, medium): no escape, containment-failure or control-line modelling.
5. Smoke/air quality (R3, medium): no smoke-dispersion or permit modelling; burn-weather-feasible days are not permit days.
6. Ecology (R4, low): habitat and vegetation-specific effects of the strip pattern are not modelled.
7. Feasibility (R6, low): about 145 burn-weather-feasible days per year on synthetic_v1 (sd 22.5; 121-176 over 2021-2025), concentrated in Apr-May and Sep-Oct (Jul 7.0, Aug 8.4, Dec 0.8 days/month). Plan build-out across a few seasons, and re-run against the real site before any scheduling.

Net: this is the most direction-robust option on the primary objective (burned area), with an unresolved, scenario-specific asset-protection weak spot. Choosing it over S4-8ab95d is a risk-tolerance decision for the approver.
